### 1. Scene
A mixed meal: creamy lettuce-and-egg salad, a tomato-sauced cheesy bake (probably pasta), and small portions of rice, broccoli, and other cooked vegetables.

### 2. Vessel
A rounded-square dinner plate, approximately **27 cm across**. Using a 27 cm circular equivalent:
**Area = 3.14 × 13.5² ≈ 573 cm².**

### 3–7. Items, area, volume, weight, and energy
The food appears to cover approximately **64%** of the plate. Dressing coats the salad, so its area overlaps the lettuce rather than adding to coverage.

| Visible item | Plate area | Area × height = gross volume | Bulk density | Weight | kcal/100 g | Energy |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Lettuce | 27% | 155 × 2.5 = 388 ml | 0.18 | 70 g | 15 | 11 kcal |
| Egg pieces in salad | 4% | 23 × 1.0 = 23 ml | 0.95 | 22 g | 155 | 34 kcal |
| Creamy dressing | Overlapping lettuce | 155 × 0.12 = 19 ml | 1.0 | 19 g | 450 | 86 kcal |
| Tomato-sauced cheesy pasta/bake | 18% | 103 × 1.8 = 185 ml | 0.8 | 149 g | 170 | 253 kcal |
| Broccoli | 7% | 40 × 2.0 = 80 ml | 0.6 | 48 g | 35 | 17 kcal |
| Cooked rice | 3% | 17 × 1.0 = 17 ml | 0.8 | 14 g | 130 | 18 kcal |
| Other cooked vegetables, including tomato | 5% | 29 × 1.5 = 44 ml | 0.6 | 26 g | 60 | 16 kcal |

The bake’s energy estimate includes its visible tomato sauce and cheese; the cooked vegetables allow for a little cooking fat.

### 8. Sanity check
**Estimated total: 348 g and approximately 435 kcal.** This is plausible for a partly covered dinner plate with a substantial salad, a modest baked entrée, and only a spoonful of rice. The bake’s identity and dressing amount are the main uncertainties.
